data.title: India's ICICI Bank Q2 profit rises 20.1%, beats estimates
data.description:
By Ashwin Manikandan

Indian private lender ICICI Bank reported a higher-than-expected profit for its second quarter on Saturday, driven by stronger loan demand and lower provisions for bad loans.

The country's second-largest private lender by market capitalisation posted a standalone net profit of 148.43 billion Indian rupees ($1.56 billion) for the three months ended September, compared with 123.59 billion rupees a year earlier.

Analysts had expected a profit of 142.51 billion rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Indian lenders have seen strong loan growth during the quarter across both corporate and retail segments.

ICICI Bank's net interest income rose 17.7% to 253.39 billion rupees, aided by a 30% increase in total loans. Deposits grew 27.1% from a year earlier.

Its net interest margin, a key measure of profitability, narrowed to 4.18% from 4.36% in the previous quarter.

Funds kept aside for potential bad loans and other losses fell 6.9% to 8.51 billion rupees.

The bank's other income, which includes income from bonds and other investments, rose 6.2% to 80.47 billion rupees amid volatile currency and debt markets.

The lender's asset quality improved, with the gross non-performing asset ratio at 1.20% at the end of September, compared with 1.38% in the prior three months.

($1 = 94.9600 Indian rupees)

data.title: Indian state food safety authority names Blinkit, Reliance executives in expired food probe
data.description:
By Arpan Chaturvedi

India's food safety authority has named officials of Reliance Group entities and of Eternal’s Blinkit and Hyperpure units, including Blinkit CEO Albinder Dhindsa, in a probe over expired food products that have allegedly re-entered the food supply chain, according to case documents reviewed by Reuters.

The Food and Drug Administration of Maharashtra state, home to Mumbai, has led a crackdown on food safety under its chief Tukaram Mundhe, 51, including shutting down some of Mumbai’s most popular eateries as well as outlets of Domino’s and Pizza Hut for poor hygiene. The state agency has also suspended the permit of a McDonald’s outlet.

The latest case, which has led to a police complaint by the food safety authority, involves large retail and quick-commerce companies, which sell products to millions of households in the world’s most populous country.

Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration, according to the documents reviewed by Reuters, said its officials visited some warehouses of Reliance Retail, Reliance Consumer and Zomato Hyperpure, and that company officials could not provide verifiable proof that disposal of expired food was actually carried out by their contractors.

"The disposal agencies ... do not destroy the stock," the case document alleged.

In the case of a Zomato Hyperpure warehouse, a company representative named a contractor as its disposal agency which FDA officials could not trace, according to the documents.

Reliance and Blinkit did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

"Any attempt to divert expired, damaged or consumer-rejected food products meant for destruction back into the market is a serious matter that demands strict scrutiny and accountability," Maharashtra's FDA chief Tukaram Mundhe told Reuters.

"No company, brand, business or individual is above the law when it comes to food safety."

INDIA'S INTENSIFYING CRACKDOWN

Reliance Retail and Reliance Consumer are part of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s business group. Zomato’s Hyperpure is a unit of Eternal that also runs food delivery service Zomato and quick commerce business Blinkit.

The FDA probe said it found a pattern where large retail and quick commerce distribution warehouses handed over expired and customer-rejected packages of food to contractors who passed the food to unlicensed sorting yards. These sorting yards then separated out saleable-looking packets, which eventually reached other retailers and the consumer market, according to case documents from the probe.

"The chain thus runs from company warehouse to disposal agency, unlicensed yard, broker, retailer and consumer."

The Maharashtra FDA on Thursday suspended the licences of five establishments in the state — three Reliance and two Eternal entities, the case documents said.

Enforcement of food safety laws has traditionally been weak in India and the recent round of extensive crackdowns has garnered large-scale public support.

In August, Indian authorities raided an illegal operation in Mumbai that faked expiry dates and nutritional information on original food products manufactured by PepsiCo , Nestle , Coca-Cola and Unilever, so they could be exported to other countries.

data.title: Judge Rejects Gemini And CFTC Bid To Overturn $5 Million Settlement
data.description:
TL;DR: A federal judge has rejected a joint attempt by Gemini and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to overturn the exchange’s $5 million settlement. The decision leaves the existing judgment in place despite the regulator’s changed approach to cryptocurrency enforcement.

Gemini has failed in an unusual attempt to undo a regulatory settlement, despite having the very agency that brought the original case on its side.

US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein rejected a joint motion by the exchange and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission seeking to vacate a consent judgment entered in January 2025.

The settlement arose from allegations that Gemini misled the regulator during its review of a proposed Bitcoin futures product in 2017. Gemini agreed to pay a $5 million penalty and accepted a permanent injunction.

When Regulators Change Their Minds

The CFTC subsequently reconsidered the original enforcement case as its digital asset priorities evolved. Together with Gemini, it asked the court to revisit the settlement.

That is a very different situation from the more familiar legal battle in which an exchange disputes a regulator’s allegations. This time, both parties wanted relief from the court’s earlier judgment.

But a change in enforcement policy does not automatically erase a final court order. The judge found that the arguments presented did not satisfy the legal standards for reopening the settlement.

The decision is significant for other cryptocurrency businesses hoping that a more accommodating federal regulatory environment might undo historical enforcement outcomes.

What Changes For Gemini?

In the immediate term, very little. The settlement remains in effect and the court has not imposed a new fine.

The wider message is more important: courts retain control of their judgments, even when a regulatory agency changes its view of a case.

Washington’s approach to cryptocurrency may have become more favourable, but companies cannot assume that previously approved settlements will disappear alongside the political circumstances in which they were reached.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: IDBI Bank stake sale: FinMin cites High Court ruling, Budget speeches to reject irregularity claims
data.description:
The Finance Ministry on Saturday clarified that there was no illegality in the approval process for the stake sale in IDBI Bank.

“The legislative history of the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, the judicial pronouncement of the Delhi High Court and successive Union Budget Speeches collectively demonstrate the evolution of the Government’s policy towards the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank,” the Ministry said in a statement. On Wednesday, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved 10955230 Canada Inc. as the Strategic Buyer for this Transaction for a purchase consideration of over Rs 52800 crore for the acquisition of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank Ltd, comprising 30.48 per cent equity shareholding held by the GoI and 30.24 per cent equity shareholding held by the LIC.

data.title: ICICI Bank Q2 results: Net profit rises 20% to Rs 14,843 crore, beats estimates; NII up 18%
data.description:
ICICI Bank on Saturday reported a 20.1 percent year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 14,843 crore for the second quarter of FY27, beating market expectations. The private sector lender also reported stronger-than-expected growth in net interest income (NII).

The bank's net profit exceeded the CNBC TV18 poll estimate of Rs 14,280 crore, which had projected a 16 percent year-on-year increase. The reported profit was approximately 3.9 percent higher than the estimate.

Net interest income, the difference between interest earned and interest paid, increased 17.7 percent year-on-year to Rs 25,338.7 crore, compared with the poll estimate of Rs 24,811 crore. The reported NII was approximately 2.1 percent above expectations.

The results indicated stronger-than-anticipated growth in both profitability and core interest income during the July-September quarter.

ICICI Bank share price

ICICI Bank shares closed 0.55 percent higher at Rs 1,397 on Friday, ahead of the quarterly earnings announcement. The stock has gained 4.4 percent so far in 2026, outperforming the benchmark Nifty 50, which has declined 11.5 percent during the same period. The bank's market capitalisation stood at approximately Rs 10.03 lakh crore at Friday's close.

data.title: Dan Ives Calls CoreWeave Sell-Off A ‘False Narrative’ — Sees Buying Opportunity With AI Demand Accelerating As CRWV Stock Sees Worst Week In 11 Months
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ives said he views the recent pressure on CoreWeave and other AI infrastructure stocks as a buying opportunity, pointing to the company's demand and backlog as reasons to look beyond the near-term volatility.
  • He added that he sees a major disconnect between the market's concerns and the underlying demand picture.
  • Ives said his recent trip to South Korea reinforced his conviction that demand across the AI hardware ecosystem continues to accelerate, particularly in memory.

CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV) shares are facing their worst week in nearly a year as investor concerns over the AI infrastructure company's debt load and rising borrowing costs intensify.

But Yorkville Ives Partner and Senior Managing Director analyst Dan Ives sees the recent sell-off as an overreaction. Ives argued during an interview with Bloomberg on Friday that the broader AI demand story remains intact even as investors reassess the economics of debt-heavy data center companies.

CoreWeave shares closed nearly 12% lower on Friday, falling about 1% further during the afterhours session. CoreWeave shares are now down over 25% this week, which is the worst weekly decline since a roughly 26% fall in November 2025.

CoreWeave Sell-Off Is A ‘False Narrative,’ Says Ives

Ives said he views the recent pressure on CoreWeave and other AI infrastructure stocks as a buying opportunity, pointing to the company's demand and backlog as reasons to look beyond the near-term volatility, while adding that he sees a major disconnect between the market's concerns and the underlying demand picture.

“When you think about what's happening in CoreWeave, given the worries in terms of the debt and what's happened with CDS spreads, I view it as similar to ‘SaaS apocalypse’ earlier this year,” he said.

While Ives acknowledged that higher interest rates could create challenges, he argued that the strength of AI demand ultimately outweighs those concerns.

“I'm not saying there's not some issues in terms as rates go higher. But given the demand, given backlog, I think this is ultimately a false narrative,” he said, while noting that the sharp decline in AI-related stocks has created an opportunity for investors.

AI Demand Is Accelerating, Ives Says

Ives said his recent trip to South Korea reinforced his conviction that demand across the AI hardware ecosystem continues to accelerate, particularly in memory.

“Memory, if I look at chips, we've seen demand accelerate 30%, 40% over the last 60 and 90 days,” he said.

For Ives, that acceleration is an important signal for the broader AI trade. He expects upcoming earnings from hyperscalers and other technology companies to provide another test of whether the massive spending cycle is continuing.

“So what that speed boost is showing is that this is all accelerating in terms as it plays out. That to me, continues to be the best barometer for what we're seeing,” he said.

He argued that investors should focus less on near-term volatility and more on whether demand for AI infrastructure continues to build.

“And I think we're going to see that in earnings relative to the hyperscalers, relative to broader tech. Focus on demand and demand is telling you we are in the third inning relative to this AI game,” he added.

Ives also acknowledged that political opposition could prevent some data center projects from moving forward, estimating that 5% to 10% could ultimately be rejected or delayed. But he said that would not fundamentally derail the AI infrastructure buildout.

Even with that potential pushback, he argued that the scale of the remaining opportunity is enormous, with data center spending continuing to have a broad impact across the technology sector.

“But still to that point, you're going to have 800 to 1,000 data centers out there,” Ives said, adding that capital spending could have a “6 to 7x multiplier” relative to the rest of tech, which he said remains central to his core AI thesis.

Jefferies Says CoreWeave Sell-Off Is Overdone

According to TheFly, Jefferies is also pushing back against the recent pressure on CoreWeave, with analyst Brent Thill maintaining a ‘Buy’ rating and a $150 price target on the stock.

Thill said the market's reaction to rising yields on CoreWeave's unsecured debt has been too harsh and does not reflect the company's underlying fundamentals.

“While future funding costs could rise, short-duration deals at about $40 million per MW more than offset this,” the firm said in a research note.

Jefferies consequently views the recent decline in CoreWeave shares as excessive.

What Retail Investors Think About CRWV Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around CoreWeave trended in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

CRWV stock is down 14% year-to-date and 57% over the past 12 months. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 18% over the past 12 months, while the Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) is up 15%.

data.title: Tata Motors' September sales: Nexon beats Punch as Sierra gains, Tiago and Harrier slip | Check full sales break-up
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Tata Motors in the month of September registered a sale of 68,810 units for passenger vehicles, compared with 59,667 units a year earlier. This is a sharp 15.32% growth adding 9,143 units over the year-ago month. Sales also increased 5.45% over the 65,253 units recorded in August 2026.

However, the growth is not even for all of its models. The Nexon retained its position as the company's best-selling model, while the Sierra and Curvv recorded month-on-month gains. On the other hand, Tiago, Harrier, and Altroz reported declines.

India's largest car maker Maruti Suzuki saw its domestic passenger vehicle dispatches jump 37 per cent to 1,81,838 units last month. Tata Motors PV emerged as the second-largest player. M&M recorded 14 per cent growth in wholesales with 64,092 units, while Hyundai's domestic wholesales grew 10.9 per cent to 57,166 units.

Passenger vehicle dispatches in the domestic market are estimated to have grown around 21 per cent to 4.60 lakh units in September, with all major carmakers posting double-digit growth.

The volume growth comes as carmakers ramped up supplies to dealerships ahead of the start of peak festival season in October, while demand remained healthy. The growth also comes on a low base in last September, when sales were hit for almost 22 days ahead of GST 2.0 rollout.

The industry is estimated to have dispatched close to 4.60 lakh units during this September. "For the month of September, the industry (wholesale volume) would be around 4.60 lakh units," Maruti Suzuki India Senior Executive Officer Partho Banerjee told reporters on Thursday.

"This should be growth of around 20-21 per cent [YoY]...Last year's number was around 3.78 lakh units."

data.title: Your Insurer Is Cutting Your Medicare Advantage Plan. Here's What to Do. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Janna Herron

Insurers that offer Medicare Advantage (MA) healthcare plans have been scaling back plans or eliminating them altogether, leaving millions of retirees in the lurch.

Indeed, many of the people who pick a Medicare Advantage plan during open enrollment that runs from Oct. 15 to Dec. 7 may only be in that plan for a year or two before it, too, goes away.

If you are one of the more than 35 million seniors enrolled in Medicare Advantage, here's what you need to know if your coverage suddenly changes or disappears.

How is Medicare Advantage different?

Unlike traditional Medicare, which is accepted by almost all doctors and hospitals, Medicare Advantage operates much like employer-provided insurance. You pay lower costs if you stay within a network of doctors and providers, and pay higher out-of-network charges if you seek care elsewhere.

The lure for many Medicare Advantage plans is you pay no monthly premium, though you still must pay your monthly Medicare premium to the Social Security Administration. By contrast, if you use traditional Medicare and supplemental, or Medigap, insurance, you will pay a private insurance premium in addition to your Medicare premium.

Medicare Advantage can save you money if you stay well. But if you get sick, you often have to pay substantial deductibles and copays, which can make MA more expensive than traditional Medicare plus supplemental insurance. You also may need to get prior authorizations from your insurer before beginning a new treatment or undergoing a recommended procedure.

Why are plan terminations happening?

In 2026, 2.6 million seniors saw their Medicare Advantage plans terminated, representing 13% of enrollees in MA plans with drug coverage, according to a KFF analysis. That was more than double the percentage from the year before. The percentage excludes seniors enrolled in MA special needs plans, plans without prescription drug coverage and those with employer coverage.

This year has seen similar moves from larger insurers like Humana, UnitedHealthcare and Molina Healthcare along with smaller plan providers such as Clear Spring Health and Presbyterian Health.

Insurers say costs for offering these plans continue to increase. Seniors are seeking healthcare services at higher rates and certain drug prices keep rising.

At the same time, federal payments for offering these plans are increasing at a slower pace, squeezing insurers' profit margins. And now, due to a federal rule change, insurers are footing a larger portion of prescription drug costs after enrollees exceed their out-of-pocket spending limit.

"Insurance companies are now deciding, 'We don't want to just lose our shirts all day long. Let's take our ball and go home,'" said Melinda Caughill, co-founder of 65 Incorporated, which provides Medicare consulting services.

What can MA seniors do?

If your insurer is getting rid of your plan, it must send you a notice. Right now — with Medicare open enrollment season heating up — it may be easy to miss it.

"People are going to be absolutely inundated with advertisements [and] mailings to try to persuade people to enroll in plans," said David Lipschutz, co-director of law and policy for the Center for Medicare Advocacy. "So sometimes the official notifications from someone's actual plan can get lost in the shuffle."

If you do nothing after getting the notice, you will be enrolled in a replacement plan. But you can also select a new Medicare Advantage plan that fits you best. The key is to make sure your preferred physicians and provider networks along with your prescription medicines are covered by any new MA plan you sign up for.

Another option is switching to traditional Medicare. That has its own issues, such as pricey or even denied Medigap plans, the supplemental policies that cover the 20% of medical costs that traditional Medicare doesn't pay.

If your current MA plan is ceasing altogether or your insurer is pulling out of your area, you should get a right to purchase a Medigap plan without undergoing any underwriting, according to Lipschutz. That means you can't get denied or charged more because of a health condition.

But if your MA plan is merging into another plan in the same area by the same insurer, that doesn't necessarily trigger the right to purchase a Medigap plan without underwriting, Lipschutz said, unless you live in the four states — Connecticut, Massachusetts, Maine and New York — that require guaranteed Medigap issue rights.

The notice you receive should spell out if you get that Medigap purchase right.

Using the nuclear option

What happens if you don't qualify for a Medigap purchase right, but the remaining MA plans don't cover your specific doctors, hospitals or treatments — especially if you are sick? You might want to consider going nuclear.

That means moving completely out of your Medicare Advantage insurer's network — oftentimes to another state, Caughill said. The move allows you to get a guaranteed right to get a Medigap policy without underwriting.

"That's why we call it the nuclear option," she said, "because you have to move."

Caughhill helped four clients this year execute this strategy after the Mayo Clinic, which provides many cancer treatments, stopped taking Medicare Advantage plans.

"For some people it's a matter of life and death," she said.

Where to get help

If your current plan is eliminated or merged, the task of finding a new plan may feel insurmountable, especially given the number of options to compare.

There are places that can help beyond the private Medicare consultants. Lipschutz recommends that seniors contact their state health insurance assistance program, also known as SHIP. You can also reach Medicare's customer support by calling 1-800-MEDICARE.

"Many more people use agents and brokers, some of whom are aboveboard," Lipschutz said. "But some are chasing commissions and steer people towards products that are best for the agent rather than the beneficiary."

data.title: Trump faults aides as Republican midterm prospects dim
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump's blame focuses on Blair as others turn on Wiles
  • President questions campaign spending, redistricting push
  • White House calls criticism 'baseless speculation'

By Nandita Bose, Bo Erickson and Steve Holland

President Donald Trump is blaming senior aides and political operatives for a faltering midterm strategy, questioning campaign spending, faulting redistricting and second-guessing candidate choices as Republicans fight to retain control of Congress, said three people familiar with internal discussions.

Trump is not on the November 3 ballot but repeatedly tells supporters to pretend that he is, hoping to mobilize voters who might otherwise skip the election. He has embarked on a frenetic campaign schedule while largely avoiding acknowledging his own role in shaping the strategy and how his unpopularity is weighing on Republican candidates in competitive races.

Much of the friction has centered on James Blair, the longtime aide who runs Trump's super PAC MAGA Inc., and White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, who until now had largely escaped criticism. Trump has faulted Blair's handling of campaign funds, while some White House officials and allies have questioned Wiles' oversight of the political operation.

As Trump questions why campaign spending has failed to improve Republican polling numbers, his advisers are also blaming one another. Wiles has pointed to Blair, while Blair has faulted the White House legislative affairs team, one of the people said.

"What's really happening is a circular firing squad," the person said.

Opinion polls suggest Democrats will win the House of Representatives, while the Senate remains too close to call. Losing the House would hamper Trump's legislative agenda in the final two years of his term and give Democrats subpoena power to investigate his administration.

Trump defended Wiles on Friday, calling her "smart" and "tough" and saying she would remain in her job. "Susie is here, and she's going to be here for a long time," he said.

White House spokesman Davis Ingle rejected the sources' characterization, saying they were "armchair experts peddling their baseless speculation." Wiles did not respond to a request for comment.

TRUMP HAS LONG DISTANCED HIMSELF FROM POLITICAL SETBACKS

Trump has long sought to distance himself from political setbacks. He refused to accept his defeat in the 2020 election and said ahead of the 2022 midterm results that he deserved "all the credit" if Republicans won but "should not be blamed at all" if they lost. More recently, he has reminded audiences that the president's party typically struggles in midterm elections.

But Trump helped devise and drive some of the strategies he is now questioning, including the redistricting effort and candidate choices shaped by his personal loyalties or grievances. His approval rating is at the lowest point of his presidency, weighed down by voter concern over high prices and dissatisfaction with the Iran war.

Trump's frustrations with his political team spilled into public view after Blair and Chris LaCivita, who co-managed Trump's 2024 campaign, traveled in early October to Republika Srpska, a self-governing region of Bosnia. The New York Times reported the men received substantial payments to advise the regional government ahead of local elections.

Trump distanced himself from both men, describing them as "outside consultants" in an October 7 Truth Social post and warning that if he found a conflict of interest, he would "terminate them, immediately!"

Senior White House officials questioned why Blair was taking on lucrative work overseas when he was supposed to be overseeing the final stretch of the Republican campaign, three people said.

One person said Wiles approved the trip without informing Trump, raising questions about how closely she was overseeing his political advisers.

For Trump, the larger concern is that Blair's outside work has distracted him from his political responsibilities, two people said.

In a statement, Blair said: "All of this mudslinging is ridiculous, and counterproductive. President Trump and me are focused on helping Republicans win in November. Every other Republican should be doing the same."

In a separate statement, LaCivita said: "President Trump and his team are and always have been focused on the midterms. That's demonstrated through the money, message and motivation that the president is bringing on the road and all year. Sniping from unnamed cowards who've never been in a fight is not worth responding to."

$200 MILLION AND REDISTRICTING

With Trump asking why Republican polling in pivotal races has not improved despite MAGA Inc.'s campaign spending, which public records put at $200 million so far, it remains unclear whether he will approve more spending before the election, one of the sources said.

Trump also has pressed political aides and advisers in the past week to explain why the redistricting effort he personally pushed has failed to deliver more clear-cut Republican gains, two sources said.

Texas is a particular concern. Republicans redrew the state's congressional map to gain seats, but the strategy relies in part on Hispanic voters turning out as they did for the 2024 election. Opinion polls suggest that support may be difficult to replicate amid concerns about the cost of living and Trump's handling of the economy. Some Republicans fear the new boundaries could backfire, leaving incumbents more vulnerable instead of giving the party an advantage.

"The redistricting diced up the Trump voters too much," one of the sources said.

Trump had said Blair was expected to return to the White House after the midterms, describing his departure as a "short leave of absence." But two sources said his return was now unlikely. "He's not coming back. That is not happening," one of them said.

It was less clear how things would play out for Wiles, who played a central role in Trump's 2024 victory and has been credited by Trump allies and aides with bringing greater discipline to his White House in his second term.

Trump "may be annoyed at certain things but she has effectively kept that machine going," a fourth source close to the White House said.

data.title: Exotic species appear off California thanks to an unusually strong El Niño
data.description:
Key points:
  • Exotic tropical species migrating further north because of El Niño
  • Weather phenomenon followed extended marine heat wave
  • Fishermen love it, but kelp beds harmed and ecosystem altered

By Daniel Trotta and Matt Silverstein

The longfin bigeye fish was spotted in California for the first time last month, and the first sea turtles of any kind nested on California beaches. Meanwhile, a venomous yellow-bellied sea snake swam ashore as whale sharks and hammerheads cruised just off the coast.

Exotic species have been visiting California's shores since an unusually strong El Niño weather phenomenon arrived this year. Occurring naturally every few years, El Niño brings warm ocean water farther north, and tropical species with it, providing California with a stunning visual display that has become ever more evident with the advent of drone and video technology.

"There's kind of a buzz. Fishermen are loving it for sure. I'm as interested as anybody else. It's strange times," said Nate Jaros, vice president of animal care at the Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach.

Other visitors include flying fish and manta rays.

California had already experienced an unusual marine heat wave just before its arrival. This year's phenomenon coincided with a string of hurricanes in the eastern Pacific, fueling sea level rise and large waves that have destroyed homes and denuded some Southern California beaches of sand. Preparing for more effects to come this winter, California has declared a state of emergency.

But it has provided a bounty for businesses like Dana Wharf Sportfishing & Whale Watching. Co-owner Donna Kalez said anglers have pulled in 5,000 yellowfin tuna this year, compared to 2 a year ago. They are also landing wahoo and dorado, also known as mahi-mahi, a green fish with a blunt head giving it the profile of a bulldozer.

"Dorado is very exciting because they're very acrobatic, so they jump out of the water. We catch them off kelp paddies, and it's a thrill," Kalez said.

Experts expect conditions to mostly return to normal after El Niño, a natural phenomenon predating human-caused climate change, passes next year. The greatest short-term harm may be to kelp, which thrives in colder waters and provides habitat for multiple species, experts say.

"It’s good for some sharks and probably bad for others," said Chris Lowe, director of the Shark Lab at California State University, Long Beach. "For animals that can't move, that's a bigger problem, right? Most sharks that are highly mobile. They can simply move."

The yellow-bellied sea snake may have venomous fangs but cannot swim like a large shark. When an apparently sick one swam ashore in Orange County in September, a beachgoer used a palm frond to lift it off the sand and drop it in the sea. Jaros said that based on cellphone video he had little doubt it was the yellow-bellied sea snake, Hydrophis platurus.

There have only been six or seven confirmed sightings in California, said William Ludt, associate curator of ichthyology at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County. The last confirmed sighting came during the El Niño of 2015-2016, he said.

Exotic sharks such as the whale shark — a gentle giant and the largest fish on Earth — and the more menacing-looking hammerheads venture into California waters during El Niño. Both have been spotted recently. Lowe said a white shark nursery reappeared for the first time since 2011 in Santa Monica Bay, where juveniles frolic without bothering humans.

Ludt said the aptly named longfin bigeye fish species was recorded for the first time in California this year when an angler caught one on the Venice Fishing Pier in Los Angeles. When two olive ridley sea turtle nests were found on a pair of Orange County beaches in September, they marked the first-ever recorded nest for any sea turtle species on the US West Coast, according to the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The first was discovered by a beachgoer in Seal Beach on September 16, the second by lifeguards in neighboring Huntington Beach three days later, officials said.

And other new species may yet arrive.

"We still aren't fully through it," Ludt said. "It's still very much ongoing."

data.title: Circle’s Allaire says stablecoin issuer looking to enter 40 developing markets: Report
data.description:
Stablecoin issuer Circle is seeking to enter about 40 developing markets, according to the company’s CEO and ​chairman, Jeremy Allaire.

“We’re kind of going through an inflection point...a transition right now, ‌and that transition is essentially moving from the early adopter phase of blockchain technology into the mainstream scaling phase,” Allaire told Reuters, speaking Friday on the sidelines of the IMF and World Bank meetings ​in Bangkok.

Markets in Southeast Asia, Latin America, Africa and the Middle East are experiencing increasing demand for stablecoins as businesses and individuals seek to enter the internet-based economic system, Allaire reportedly said.

Cointelegraph reported on Aug. 24 that analysts at Bernstein were bullish on Circle, foreseeing a new growth cycle for its USDC stablecoin may provide a significant boost for the company over the next 12 months.

Bernstein said the next phase of stablecoin growth could be driven by several factors, including renewed momentum in crypto markets, greater US regulatory clarity, tokenized capital markets and growing adoption of stablecoins for payments. The analysts also pointed to early signs of stablecoin use in payments made by AI agents.

Although USDC remains the second-largest dollar-backed stablecoin by market capitalization, well behind Tether’s USDt (USDT), it has gained significant ground in transaction activity. Bernstein said USDC’s share of adjusted stablecoin transaction volume rose from about 40% in 2025 to more than 60% so far in 2026, overtaking USDt by that measure.

On Sept. 8, Cointelegraph reported that Circle had agreed to acquire Singapore-based cross-border payments platform Tazapay in a $400 million all-stock deal expected to close in 2027.
