data.title: ‘AI Can Help India Cut Power Peaks Without Building More Capacity’
data.description:
Smart-meter analytics, behavioural demand response, battery storage and flexible electricity consumption could help distribution utilities manage rising demand while improving renewable energy integration

India’s power distribution utilities could use artificial intelligence (AI), smart-meter data and consumer-led demand response to reduce peak electricity demand and ease pressure on existing grid infrastructure, experts said at the Central Electricity Authority’s (CEA) 53rd Foundation Day event in New Delhi on 15 October, 2026.

The approach could help utilities manage rising cooling loads during extreme heat, integrate more renewable energy and defer the need for additional capacity by shifting flexible electricity consumption away from peak hours. Demand response involves encouraging or enabling consumers to adjust when and how they use electricity in response to grid requirements.

As renewable energy generation expands, AI-based forecasting and better use of consumption data could help utilities align electricity demand with periods of higher solar generation while managing evening peaks. India has already established a foundation for demand-side management. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) has documented initiatives undertaken by distribution companies, with an estimated potential to reduce demand by around 13,000 MW and save 28 billion units of electricity annually, according to figures presented at the CEA event.

Consumer Behaviour And Storage Can Ease Peak Demand

The experience of Tata Power Delhi Distribution Limited (Tata Power-DDL) illustrates how consumer participation can influence peak demand. The utility began experimenting with automated demand response in 2014, initially targeting industrial consumers. Early trials achieved around 7 MW of peak-load reduction across seven to eight events, but concerns about operational control and the limited effectiveness of financial incentives constrained participation. The utility subsequently shifted towards behavioural demand response, allowing consumers to control their electricity use while receiving alerts about anticipated peak periods.

Dwijadas Basak, Chief Executive Officer of Tata Power-DDL, said the programme had expanded to approximately 2.2 lakh consumers. He reported around 500 MW of cumulative load reduction across 17 events conducted during May, June and July. “The motivation that the customers are getting is the sustainability, the pride that they are doing something for the nation, for the environment, for the world,” Basak said, highlighting the role of awareness and recognition in encouraging participation. The experience suggests that demand response cannot depend exclusively on financial incentives. Regular communication, timely alerts and an understanding of consumer behaviour are also necessary to sustain participation.

Abhishek Ranjan, Chief Executive Officer of BSES Rajdhani Power Limited (BRPL), highlighted the challenges of managing residential cooling demand during Delhi’s hottest periods, when consumers may be unwilling or unable to reduce air-conditioning use. Battery storage at distribution transformer and grid-substation levels could help address these constraints by supplying electricity during short periods of high demand. Rooftop solar, scheduled electric-vehicle charging and energy-efficient appliances could provide additional flexibility. Ranjan also highlighted the importance of having reliable control over demand-response resources when managing real-time network conditions.

AI Forecasting And Standardisation Can Enable Scale

AI could strengthen demand-response programmes by helping utilities analyse smart-meter readings, weather conditions and consumption patterns to forecast demand more accurately. Appliance-level analysis could help identify flexible loads across residential, commercial and industrial consumers, allowing utilities to estimate how much demand can realistically be shifted during peak periods. Dr Mahesh Patankar, Founder and Managing Director of MP Ensystems Advisory, highlighted the potential to turn smart-meter infrastructure into a continuous source of information for electricity planning.

By combining historical consumption data with weather forecasts and appliance-level insights, utilities could improve predictions of daily, weekly and seasonal demand. Such analysis could also help identify where interventions would deliver the greatest benefits. However, forecasting alone will not resolve every grid constraint. Distribution companies also need common systems to measure outcomes and replicate successful programmes across regions. Prince Dhawan, IAS, Executive Director of REC Limited, identified standardised digital infrastructure as a way to address this challenge.

“If you have to build everything every time from scratch, then nothing will ever scale up,” Dhawan said. For India, the next step is to move from isolated demonstrations towards demand-response programmes that deliver measurable and repeatable results. AI can help utilities anticipate peaks, but meaningful reductions will depend on identifying flexible loads, engaging consumers and establishing systems that allow demand response to operate reliably at scale. As renewable generation increases and electricity consumption patterns evolve, managing when power is used could become as important as expanding how much electricity the country can generate.

Sonali Chawhan

BW Reporters

The author is a Trainee Correspondent at BW Businessworld.

data.title: AXISCADES Technologies Appoints Uttam Kumar Bhageria As CFO-Designate
data.description:
Bhageria will take over as Chief Financial Officer on 1 January 2027, following the superannuation of incumbent Group CFO Shashidhar SK on 31 December 2026

AXISCADES Technologies has appointed Uttam Kumar Bhageria as Chief Financial Officer (CFO)-Designate, effective 21 October 2026. He will take over as Chief Financial Officer and Key Managerial Personnel (KMP) on 1 January 2027, following the superannuation of the current Group Chief Financial Officer and KMP, Shashidhar SK, on 31 December 2026.

The appointment was recommended by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and the Audit Committee and approved by the Board of Directors on 16 October 2026.

Bhageria will serve as CFO-Designate until 31 December 2026, before assuming the CFO role on 1 January 2027. The transition period will allow for a handover ahead of Shashidhar SK’s superannuation at the end of December.

Bhageria has more than two decades of experience in strategic finance across listed companies, multinational organisations and promoter-led businesses.

His professional background includes leading an acquisition valued at Rs 3,000 crore, driving a fivefold increase in market capitalisation through strategic initiatives, and managing corporate restructuring and capital market activities.

He has also worked with global consulting firms BCG and McKinsey on transformation and diversification projects.

Regulatory Disclosure

The appointment was disclosed under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

According to the disclosure, Bhageria is not related to any existing director of the company. The board meeting on 16 October commenced at 4:30 pm IST and concluded at 5:00 pm IST.

data.title: Iveco Shareholders Approve Delisting, Restructuring Plans For Tata Motors Deal
data.description:
The resolutions provide for Iveco’s conversion into a private limited liability company following delisting and a potential post-offer demerger if Tata Motors secures at least 80 per cent of common shares

Iveco Group shareholders have approved all resolutions related to Tata Motors’ proposed acquisition of the Italian commercial vehicle manufacturer, reducing the minimum share acceptance threshold from 95 per cent to 80 per cent and clearing a key hurdle for the transaction.

The resolutions were approved at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) held in Amsterdam on Friday, Iveco said in a statement. The approval fulfils several conditions required for Tata Motors’ acquisition vehicle to declare its voluntary public tender offer unconditional. However, the transaction remains subject to other conditions.

Tata Motors, through its subsidiary TML CV Holdings, is seeking to acquire Iveco’s commercial vehicle business. On 9 October, the Indian automaker raised its offer price from Euro 14.10 to Euro 14.40 per share, valuing the transaction at approximately Euro 3.91 billion.

The revised acceptance threshold reduces the proportion of Iveco shares Tata Motors must secure to proceed with the acquisition, potentially easing the completion of the transaction.

Shareholder Approvals

Shareholders also approved amendments to Iveco’s Articles of Association (AoA), its conversion from a publicly listed company into a private limited liability company following delisting, and the appointment of new board members, effective upon settlement.

The resolutions provide for a post-offer demerger, which the acquirer may implement if it secures at least 80 per cent of Iveco’s common shares. Shareholders also authorised a subsequent share sale and the potential dissolution of the existing corporate entity as part of the post-acquisition restructuring.

The EGM further approved changes to Iveco’s special voting share arrangements, including the termination of its loyalty voting structure following settlement.

The acquisition is expected to expand Tata Motors’ geographical presence and product portfolio in the global commercial vehicle market, particularly in Europe.

The voluntary public tender offer is scheduled to close on 26 October, unless extended. Completion will depend on the fulfilment of the remaining offer conditions.

data.title: Snabbit Posts Rs 168 Cr Loss In FY26 As Quick Home Services Competition Intensifies
data.description:
Snabbit reported a net loss of Rs 168 crore in FY26 on operating revenue of Rs 12.25 crore, as the two-year-old on-demand home services startup invested in customer acquisition, workforce expansion and service delivery amid intensifying competition in the quick home services market, as per a media report.

The company’s operating revenue increased from Rs 26 lakh in FY25 to Rs 12.25 crore in FY26, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC). However, its total expenses rose sharply to Rs 195 crore from Rs 6.8 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Founded in 2024 by Aayush Agarwal, Snabbit connects households with trained professionals for tasks such as cleaning, dishwashing and laundry. Customers can book services by the hour, with the platform offering fulfilment within 10 minutes.

Platform services generated Rs 10.82 crore, accounting for 88 per cent of operating revenue in FY26. The remaining revenue came from uniform sales. The company also reported Rs 14.76 crore in other income, primarily from interest earned on bank deposits.

Snabbit’s expenditure included Rs 46 crore in employee benefit costs and Rs 63 crore in expert service costs. It spent another Rs 49 crore on marketing and Rs 23.8 crore on service fulfilment. Banking charges, commissions, recruitment, legal expenses, software maintenance and other overheads contributed to total expenses of Rs 195 crore.

The company’s net loss widened from Rs 5.7 crore in FY25 to Rs 168 crore in FY26. At the unit level, Snabbit spent Rs 15.92 to generate every rupee of operating revenue.

Its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -58.45 per cent, while its EBITDA margin was -1,481.63 per cent in FY26.

Snabbit has raised more than USD 112 million to date. Its funding includes a USD 56 million Series D round backed by Susquehanna VC, Mirae Asset Venture Investments and Bertelsmann India Investments.

The startup has also reported growth in service volumes. It said it crossed 115,000 fulfilled jobs in a single day and completed four million home-help jobs during Q1 FY27. Its burn per job declined by more than Rs 100 quarter-on-quarter to below Rs 250.

Agarwal said FY26 was the company’s first full year of operations. During the year, Snabbit expanded from around 500 daily jobs across eight micro-markets to 35,000 daily jobs across more than 100 micro-markets, representing a 75-fold increase in daily jobs. It also acquired nearly one million customers and onboarded more than 20,000 experts.

The founder attributed the Rs 167.8 crore loss to investments in expansion, customer and expert acquisition, and long-term capabilities. He said FY26 financials do not reflect current economics, pointing to improvements in operating leverage and unit economics as the business built greater density across neighbourhoods.

Snabbit is competing with Urban Company’s InstaHelp and Pronto, as companies seek to build demand for on-demand household services. Urban Company’s InstaHelp completed around 1.9 million orders in July 2026, ahead of Snabbit’s 1.85 million, while Pronto crossed 1.25 million bookings.

Urban Company has also been investing in its quick home services business and has reportedly been looking to raise USD 200 million, as competition in the segment intensifies.

The companies are expanding their customer bases, building workforces and increasing fulfilment capacity. However, their ability to translate higher order volumes into sustainable earnings will depend on worker utilisation, customer acquisition costs, repeat bookings and the density of demand within individual neighbourhoods.

For Snabbit and its competitors, the challenge is to establish a business model in which bookings generate sufficient revenue to cover service delivery and operating costs. Until then, continued expansion may require further funding as the companies work towards improving unit economics.

data.title: Goldman Sachs Sells Rs 168.67 Cr Worth Of Eternal Shares To BofA Securities
data.description:
Goldman Sachs sold 53.37 lakh shares of Eternal, the parent company of Zomato and Blinkit, for Rs 168.67 crore in a block deal, with BofA Securities buying the same number of shares on October 15, according to a media report.

Exchange data show Goldman Sachs sold 53,37,584 shares at Rs 316 per share, while BofA Securities bought them at the same price. The transaction accounted for around 0.05 per cent of Eternal's paid-up equity.

The transaction follows bulk deals on August 31, when investors sold nearly Rs 3,265 crore worth of Eternal shares. BNP Paribas Financial Markets sold 5.09 crore shares worth Rs 1,670.86 crore, while Integrated Core Strategies (Asia), an affiliate of Millennium Management, sold 4.86 crore shares for Rs 1,593.96 crore.

Eternal reported revenue from operations of Rs 20,211 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 7,167 crore in the corresponding period a year earlier. Net profit increased to Rs 92 crore from Rs 25 crore in the year-ago quarter. However, profit declined from Rs 174 crore in the March quarter.

For FY26, the company's revenue from operations rose to Rs 54,364 crore from Rs 20,243 crore in FY25. Net profit, however, declined to Rs 366 crore from Rs 527 crore during the same period.

Eternal operates Zomato's food delivery business and Blinkit, its quick commerce platform. Blinkit competes with Swiggy Instamart and Zepto in India's quick commerce market, where companies are expanding their store networks to increase delivery capacity.

Eternal shares were trading at Rs 323.60 as of 9:37 am, valuing the company at a market capitalisation of Rs 3,11,947 crore.

data.title: Cult.fit Receives Sebi Observations For Rs 950 Cr IPO
data.description:
Fitness and lifestyle platform Cult.fit has received observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO), as per a media report. The company plans to raise Rs 950 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, alongside an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 17.86 crore shares by existing shareholders.

The proceeds from the fresh issue will be used to repay borrowings, establish new Cult Elite and Cult Neo fitness centres, expand Cultsport exclusive brand outlets, meet lease and rental payments for existing centres, and fund brand marketing and general corporate purposes.

According to the company's draft papers, Cult.fit operated 708 fitness centres across 77 cities in India as of March 31, 2026. Its fitness services business had nearly 9.87 lakh paid members in FY26, while its fitness products business shipped more than 42.3 lakh products during the year.

Cult.fit Revenue Rises 36% In FY26

Cult.fit operates across two main segments: fitness services and fitness products. Fitness services contributed around 70 per cent of its revenue, while fitness products accounted for the remaining 30 per cent.

The company's operating revenue increased 36.26 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,720.61 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 1,262.93 crore in FY25. It had reported operating revenue of Rs 926.66 crore in FY24.

Its adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 8.41 per cent in FY26 from -2.76 per cent in FY25, according to the draft papers.

The company operates different fitness centre formats, including Cult Elite, which combines gym workouts with instructor-led group classes, and Cult Neo, which focuses on equipment-based workouts. Its Cultsport brand sells fitness apparel, footwear, equipment and accessories.

Cult.fit also uses a technology-led platform to connect its fitness services and products businesses through its app, website and offline channels.

India’s Fitness Market Projected To Expand

The proposed IPO comes amid growth in India's organised fitness market. According to the Redseer report cited in the draft papers, the country's fitness services market was estimated at Rs 25,600 crore in CY25 and is projected to reach Rs 48,700 crore to Rs 53,100 crore by CY30.

The company's equity shares are proposed to be listed on the BSE and NSE.

Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs India Securities, Jefferies India, JM Financial and Morgan Stanley India are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

data.title: HDFC Bank reports 5% increase in Q2FY27 standalone net profit at ₹19,510 crore
data.description:
HDFC Bank reported a 5 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) increase in second quarter (Q2FY27) standalone net profit at ₹19,510 crore amid a 10 per cent growth in net interest income and a 4 per cent decline in other income.

India’s largest private sector bank, which is set to see a leadership change with Anup Bagchi, Chief of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance,set to take charge as MD & CEO for three years with effect from October 27, 2026, had logged a net profit of ₹18,641 crore in the year-ago period.

Net interest income (interest income less interest expended) rose 10 per cent y-o-y to ₹34,619 crore (₹31,551.50 crore in Q2FY26).

Other income, including commission income from non-fund based banking activities, fees, earnings from forex and derivative transactions, profit and loss (including revaluation) from investments, dividends from subsidiaries and recoveries from accounts previously written off, declined 4 per cent y-o-y to ₹13,831 crore (₹14,350 crore).

Provisions inched up 2 per cent y-o-y to ₹3,574 crore (₹3,501 crore).

Gross non-performing assets (NPAs) position improved to 1.11 per cent of gross advances as at September-end 2026 against 1.24 per cent as at September-end 2025. Net NPAs position too improved to 0.37 per cent of net advances against 0.42 per cent.

Total deposits grew by a robust 19 per cent y-o-y to stand at ₹33,27,449 crore as at September-end 2026. Advances too rose by a healthy 16 per cent y-o-y to stand at ₹31,95,566 crore as at September-end 2026.

data.title: Festive demand to drive PNB retail loan growth to 17-18%, MSME credit to grow 21%: MD&CEO Ashok Chandra
data.description:
Punjab National Bank (PNB) expects core retail loan growth to reach 17-18 per cent and micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) lending to grow around 21 per cent in the current quarter, with the festive season expected to support credit demand, Ashok Chandra, MD & CEO of Punjab National Bank, told ANI.

The bank also expects agriculture priority-sector lending to maintain its growth momentum after recording 18 per cent growth, as it looks to sustain profitability and improve asset quality in the coming quarters.

“Three areas, retail is doing very well and core retail activity like housing, vacation, mortgage loans, education loan, that is growing at more than 16 percent and I am expecting that this being the festive season, a lot of activities will happen and somewhere around 17 to 18 percent growth should happen in the core retail segment,” Chandra said.

He further added that, “Agriculture priority sector, we are growing at 18 percent and the momentum will continue in this particular quarter also. MSME, we are growing at 20 percent and I'm expecting that in this quarter around 21 percent growth will happen”.

On the bank's overall performance, Chandra said PNB had reported strong growth, asset quality and profitability in every quarter over the past two years and expected the trend to continue. “I'm fully confident that this trend is going to continue in the coming quarters also. You will see the good growth happening across these sectors in the credit. Good growth is happening in the profitability and there will be further reduction in the gross NPA, net NPA,” he said.

PNB sanctioned corporate loans worth ₹2.5 lakh crore in the first two quarters of the current financial year, compared with ₹4 lakh crore during the entire previous financial year.Chandra said the bank was replacing lower-yielding advances with higher-yielding loans, keeping corporate loan-book growth at around 10-11 per cent despite a rise in sanctions.

The strategy helped improve net interest income, with domestic net interest margin (NIM) rising by more than 10 basis points and global NIM by 8 basis points during the quarter. On interest rate, Chandra said the latest 25-basis-point repo rate hike could have a positive impact of around 7 basis points on NIM.

He said lending and deposit rates would be reviewed by the bank's Asset Liability Committee (ALCO) in the coming months, while the RBI would decide on any further rate action based on inflation and growth trends.

data.title: FSSAI initiates legal proceedings against Priyagold Biscuits maker, Dodla Dairy, Ueir Organic Foods
data.description:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSA) has initiated legal proceedings against Surya Food & Agro Ltd, which is known for Priyagold biscuits besides Dodla Dairy Ltd and Ueir Organic Foods Pvt Ltd for serious food safety violations. Also, it has issued notices to Narpadham Foods, Sun Ridges Health Carers, and Sha Kantilal Jayantilal.

“The authority maintains zero tolerance for any food safety violations or compromises on public health as per FSS Act 2006, ensuring that strict legal consequences follow for non-compliant food business operators,” the regulator said in a social media post.

In the case of Surya Food & Agro, FSSAI said that an inspection conducted, after receiving a consumer complaint, revealed “serious food safety and hygiene deficiencies.” “Bran meant for cattle feed and not intended for human consumption was being used as a raw material for Priyagold as a source of fiber,” the regulator said in a social media post. Other deficiencies included plant hygiene, pest control, raw material storage and segregation, personnel hygiene, premises maintenance, among others, it added.

“The FSSAI license of Surya Food & Agro has been suspended following serious non-compliances observed during inspection. The competent authority granted sanction for initiating prosecution against Surya Food & Agro for violations,” it noted.

Meanwhile, prosecution has been initiated against Ueir Organic Foods Pvt Ltd after a regulatory sample of Yellow Raisins-an Organic Food was found to be “unsafe due to pesticide residues exceeding prescribed limits,” Upon appeal by the FBO, the sample was sent to a Referral Laboratory, which confirmed that the Yellow Raisin sample was unsafe due to Thiamethoxam and Fluopyram metabolites exceeding the prescribed limit, the food safety regulator said.

Prosecution has also been initiated against Dodla Dairy after a regulatory sample of “Full Cream Milk” was found to be substandard as it did not conform with the milk fat specification prescribed by the regulations. “ Upon appeal by the FBO, the sample was referred to the Referral Food Laboratory, which confirmed that the sample was found to be unsafe due to presence of detergent/ caustic soda and substandard due to the milk fat below the minimum prescribed limits,” the FSSAI said in its post.

FSSAI has sent a notice to Narpadham Foods for various food safety, hygiene and licensing non-compliances. “ The FBO has been asked to review and correct any misleading health or nutrition claims on product labels and promotional materials and remove Retail category from its FSSAI license, as no retail outlet is operated. The FBO must also submit a written explanation, an action taken report and a compliance report within the stipulated time period. Failure to comply may result in suspension or cancellation of the license,” it added.

A notice has been sent to Sha Kantilal Jayantilal, after an inspection found the licensed premises were closed and details have been sought regarding its “actual business activities, the food safety regulator said.

data.title: Death toll in Sept 30 MRPL fire rises to 2
data.description:
The death toll from the September 30 fire at MRPLc’s (Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd) coker hydrotreater unit in phase III rose to two after another contract employee succumbed to injuries on October 17.

One person was killed and 12 injured in the incident on September 30. Of the 12 injured, Rajesh D’Silva, a contract employee, was admitted to hospital with 35 per cent burns on that day. Police said he succumbed to injuries on October 17.

Others with minor injuries had received outpatient treatment on September 30.

The company had earlier said that an incident involving the rupture of a cold separator operating at high pressure in the coker hydrotreater unit resulted in a fire on September 30. The battery limits of the affected unit were immediately isolated to control the situation.

In its notes to the standalone financial results for the second quarter of 2026-27, the company had informed stock exchanges that it has provisionally estimated the financial impact of the September 30 fire incident at ₹118.76 crore.

“Based on a preliminary assessment, the company has provisionally estimated the financial impact of the incident at ₹118.76 crore, comprising the estimated carrying value of the damaged Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE), corresponding to an estimated replacement value of approximately ₹225 crore and losses relating to inventories and other incidental expenses,” it said.

The company said the affected assets are adequately insured by it.

data.title: Air India extends temporary suspension of flights to Saudi Arabia until Oct 24 amid Houthi attacks
data.description:
Air India and Air India Express have extended their temporary suspension of flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam in Saudi Arabia until October 24 amid the Houthi rebels’ strikes in the West Asian country. In a travel advisory, Air India said that the bookings issued on or before October 15 with travel dates between October 9 and 25 are eligible for a one-time complimentary date change up to  November 10.

Air India stated, "In view of the prevailing situation, Air India and Air India Express have temporarily suspended flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam until 24 October 2026. We understand that these disruptions may affect our guests' travel plans and are committed to providing as much flexibility as possible during this period.”

“Guests holding confirmed Air India or Air India Express bookings issued on or before 15 October 2026, with travel dates between 9 October and 25 October 2026, are eligible for a one-time complimentary date change on their respective airline up to 10 November 2026. Guests who do not wish to rebook on the originally preferred sector for a future date may, instead, choose to rebook from an alternative station in the GCC region served by their respective airline, subject to availability,” the statement read.

The passengers can also opt for a different destination in West Asia with the airline stating, “Guests choosing the latter option are required to make their own travel arrangements to get to their preferred alternative point of departure and meet the applicable visa and entry requirements. Air India guests may rebook to or from Dubai or Doha. Air India Express guests may rebook to or from Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Bahrain, Doha, Dubai, Kuwait, Muscat, Ras Al Khaimah, Salalah or Sharjah. Guests whose flights have been cancelled may also opt for a full refund if they choose not to travel.”

“We continue to closely monitor the situation and will keep guests informed of any further updates. Our priority remains to support affected guests, minimise inconvenience, and help them continue their journeys with suitable travel options,” Air India said. Several airlines, including IndiGo and Akasa Air, have also temporarily suspended their operations in Saudi Arabia.

The disruptions come after the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, with the death toll rising to 13 after the Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed that an Indian national who had been injured in the incident died.

As the conflict escalated, Yemen's internationally recognised government on Friday accused the Houthi militia of targeting Aden International Airport with two missiles that landed near a Yemenia Airlines aircraft preparing for takeoff to Cairo, according to the country's Information Minister Moammar Al-Eryani.

data.title: New steel policy to promote circular economy, boost value addition: Industry
data.description:
The proposed National Steel Policy will promote a circular economy and boost value-added production within India, steel industry stakeholders said.

The policy, which builds a roadmap up to 2027 for the sector, also focuses on decarbonisation of the Indian steel industry, they said.

Pankaj Malhan, MD & CEO of RHI Magnesita India, said the recognition of refractory recovery and magnesite raw material security in the draft policy reflects a holistic approach to build a resilient and competitive steel ecosystem.

"The industry welcomes this policy direction and remains committed to advancing refractory recycling, circular economy initiatives, and investments in India," he said.

BMW Industries Managing Director Harsh Bansal said the policy has taken every aspect of the steel industry into consideration.

It focuses on value-added and coated steel production and lifting of secondary steel players, Bansal said.

Rajib Maitra, Partner, Deloitte India, said the policy envisages reducing the sector's average carbon emission intensity from 2.54 tCO/tcs to approximately 1.54 tCO'/tcs by 2047 through four phases.

Satish Kumar Agarwal, Chairman and Managing Director, Kamdhenu Group, said the emphasis on capacity expansion, raw-material security, technological modernisation, speciality steel and decarbonisation opens significant opportunities for integrated steel producers and secondary steel manufacturers in the country.

Deepak Kumar, Managing Director, PS Raj Steels, said that for downstream manufacturers, support for manufacturing clusters and MSMEs, which account for nearly 60 per cent of flat stainless steel capacity, will matter as much as capacity expansion at the top of the value chain.

The government has released a new steel policy to boost India's crude steel capacity to 604 million tonnes by 2047, enhance industry competitiveness and address key import challenges.

According to the draft National Steel Policy 2047, finished steel demand will rise to 505 MT by 2047, per capita consumption to 302 kg and steel exports to 45 MT.

data.title: Indian state food safety authority names Blinkit, Reliance executives in expired food probe
data.description:
By Arpan Chaturvedi

Indian food safety authorities have named officials of Reliance Group entities and of Eternal’s Blinkit and Hyperpure units, including Blinkit CEO Albinder Dhindsa, in a probe over expired food products that have allegedly re-entered the food supply chain, according to case documents reviewed by Reuters.

The Food and Drug Administration of Maharashtra state, home to Mumbai, has led a crackdown on food safety under its chief Tukaram Mundhe, 51, including shutting down some of Mumbai’s most popular eateries as well as outlets of Domino’s and Pizza Hut for poor hygiene. The state agency has also suspended the permit of a McDonald’s outlet.

The latest case, which has led to a police complaint by the food safety authority, involves large retail and quick-commerce companies, which sell products to millions of households in the world’s most populous country.

Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration, according to the documents reviewed by Reuters, said its officials visited some warehouses of Reliance Retail, Reliance Consumer and Zomato Hyperpure, and that company officials could not provide verifiable proof that disposal of expired food was actually carried out by their contractors.

"The disposal agencies ... do not destroy the stock," the case document alleged.

In the case of a Zomato Hyperpure warehouse, a company representative named a contractor as its disposal agency which FDA officials could not trace, according to the documents.

Reliance and Blinkit did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

INDIA'S INTENSIFYING CRACKDOWN

Reliance Retail and Reliance Consumer are part of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s business group. Zomato’s Hyperpure is a unit of Eternal that also runs food delivery service Zomato and quick commerce business Blinkit.

The FDA probe said it found a pattern where large retail and quick commerce distribution warehouses handed over expired and customer-rejected packages of food to contractors who passed the food to unlicensed sorting yards. These sorting yards then separated out saleable-looking packets, which eventually reached other retailers and the consumer market, according to case documents from the probe.

"The chain thus runs from company warehouse to disposal agency, unlicensed yard, broker, retailer and consumer."

The Maharashtra FDA on Thursday suspended the licences of five establishments in the state, three of Reliance and two of Eternal entities, the case documents said.

Enforcement of food safety laws has traditionally been weak in India and the recent round of extensive crackdowns has garnered large-scale public support.

In August, Indian authorities raided an illegal operation in Mumbai that faked expiry dates and nutritional information on original food products manufactured by PepsiCo , Nestle , Coca-Cola and Unilever, so they could be exported to other countries.

data.title: Bitcoin Is Jordi Visser's ‘Most Asymmetric Bet Ever’ As Tokenization Threatens To Upend Hedge Funds
data.description:
Key points:
  • Jordi Visser called Bitcoin "the most asymmetric bet I've ever made in my life" on Galaxy's podcast on Friday.
  • He said tokenization will push markets toward round-the-clock trading, so prime brokers could remark on hedge fund portfolios on weekends when liquidity is thin.
  • He pointed to Korea's plan for full tokenization by 2027, saying investors would want to trade on Korean prices around the clock to hedge their US portfolios.

Wall Street veteran Jordi Visser called Bitcoin (BTC) "the most asymmetric bet I've ever made in my life," adding that the next big disruption from crypto could land on hedge funds.

Speaking on Galaxy's Galaxy Brains podcast on Friday with Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s (GLXY) Head of Firmwide Research, Visser said his Bitcoin bet was not about the next two or three years, but depended on what he thought would be “happening to all fiat assets relative to something that has no fundamentals.”

Why Tokenization Could Upend Hedge Funds?

Visser, who is a former hedge fund manager, said that hedge funds were already calling him about tokenization. "They're reaching out on what tokenization means," he said, adding that the callers were names most people would recognize.

He explained tokenization meant "the destruction of hedge funds,” because they traded around the clock. In a 24/7 market, prices would keep moving through the weekend. Visser said that meant a hedge fund's entire portfolio could be marked lower on a Sunday, when liquidity was thin, and prime brokers that lend to the fund would notice.

Lenders "know that the price is different and they know that the P&L you're going to have is different," he said. "It puts a much bigger microscope on risk management."

Why Korean Markets Matters

Visser pointed out that the Korean market could force the shift, as it wanted full tokenization by 2027, and its stock market was heavily tied to the memory chip makers at the center of the AI trade.

US hedge funds already checked Korea's KOSPI index first thing in the morning, he said. If Korean stocks traded 24/7, investors would want to hedge their US portfolios at the same time.

"So I challenge anyone who says it isn't going to happen," Visser said. "It might take longer than we all think, but again, we're at zero right now."

Bitcoin Needs A 635% Rally To Reach Visser's Price Target

Previously, Visser has made many bullish calls on Bitcoin. Last month, he said AI-driven demand and tokenization, combined with Bitcoin's scarcity, could push the apex cryptocurrency's price to $600,000 to $1 million if the crypto market expands toward $100 trillion.

Bitcoin's price was trading at $81,612, down by 0.7% during the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

For Bitcoin to reach the lower band of Visser’s prediction, it would need to rally 635% from its current levels.

data.title: Starlink Says India Infrastructure Ready, Claims Government Approvals In Place Amid Satcom Row
data.description:
Elon Musk-led company says it has worked with Indian regulators for over five years and is ready to offer high-speed internet, as Reliance Industries stresses compliance with Indian laws

Starlink, the satellite internet venture of Elon Musk-led SpaceX, has said it has built dedicated infrastructure in India with the requisite government approvals and is ready to provide high-speed internet services, amid an escalating debate over regulatory clearances and competition in the country's satellite communications market.

In a statement on Friday, the company said it had worked with Indian regulators, industry participants and telecom operators for more than five years to prepare for its entry into the Indian market. The assertion comes as the company awaits the remaining clearances required to begin commercial operations.

The latest development follows a public exchange between Starlink and Reliance Industries over the regulatory framework governing satellite broadband services in India. Reliance has welcomed competition in the sector but maintained that all operators must comply with Indian laws and regulations.

Starlink Highlights Infrastructure Investment

Starlink said its preparations for India included building dedicated ground infrastructure and developing operations to meet the country's regulatory requirements. The company has previously said it established more than 20 gateway sites comprising hundreds of antennas across India.

Lauren Dreyer, Vice-President of Business Operations at SpaceX, had said at the India Mobile Congress that Starlink had developed India-specific security controls and measures to keep Indian user data within the country.

The company has also entered into partnerships with Bharti Airtel and Reliance Jio to facilitate its prospective entry into the Indian market, subject to regulatory approvals.

Despite these preparations, Starlink's commercial launch remains contingent on the completion of the outstanding regulatory process, including security-related requirements and foreign direct investment (FDI) approval.

Reliance Emphasises Compliance With Indian Laws

Reliance Industries said on Friday that it did not fear competition from satellite communications providers, including Starlink, but stressed that all companies operating in India must adhere to the country's laws and regulations.

The exchange follows Musk's earlier allegations that unnamed business interests were obstructing Starlink's entry into India to protect their market positions. The government has rejected allegations of discrimination, stating that it follows a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunications services, including satellite communications.

The Ministry of Communications has said security assessments are under way for all three licensed satellite communications operators — Starlink, Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Reliance Jio's satellite communications arm. The companies must meet the applicable security requirements before proceeding to the next stage of regulatory approval.

Commercial Launch Awaits Regulatory Clearances

Starlink has secured a Global Mobile Personal Communications by Satellite (GMPCS) licence from the Department of Telecommunications and authorisation from the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe).

However, these approvals alone do not permit the company to commence commercial services. Security clearance, FDI approval and the completion of the spectrum assignment process remain important steps before its launch.

The Department of Telecommunications has backed an administrative allocation framework for satellite spectrum, with a proposed spectrum usage charge of 5 per cent of adjusted gross revenue. The broader framework has also involved government-level approvals and security requirements.

India's satellite broadband market is attracting interest from domestic and international players seeking to provide connectivity in remote and underserved areas. Starlink's eventual entry would add another competitor to the market, where satellite-based services are expected to complement existing terrestrial broadband and mobile networks.

data.title: Shoppers Stop Returns To Profit In Q2 FY27 As Ebitda Jumps 56% To Rs 43 Cr
data.description:
Premium beauty sales rise 18% to Rs 367 crore, while consolidated non-GAAP revenue grows 7% to Rs 1,618 crore; retailer targets debt-free status by Q3 FY27

Shoppers Stop reported a return to profitability in the second quarter of FY27, with consolidated profit after tax (PAT) reaching Rs 6 crore against a loss of Rs 7 crore in the year-ago quarter, as the retailer continued to improve operational efficiency and focus on premiumisation.

Consolidated non-GAAP revenue rose 7 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,618 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 1,507 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) increased 56 per cent to Rs 43 crore from Rs 28 crore.

On a consolidated GAAP basis, revenue stood at Rs 1,366 crore, up 9 per cent year-on-year, while Ebitda increased 22 per cent to Rs 219 crore. PAT stood at Rs 3 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 20 crore in Q2 FY26.

The company attributed the improvement to its premiumisation-led growth strategy, better operating leverage and continued execution of its Shoppers Stop 2.0 strategy. The festive season largely shifting to the third quarter also influenced the quarter's performance.

Commenting on the results, Kavindra Mishra, Managing Director and CEO of Shoppers Stop, said the company had delivered a turnaround in profitability despite the change in the festive calendar. He added that the retailer remained focused on improving profitability and achieving its target of becoming debt-free by the end of Q3 FY27.

Beauty Segment Leads Growth

The beauty business remained a key growth driver, with sales increasing 18 per cent year-on-year to Rs 367 crore. Fragrance led the segment, recording 35 per cent growth during the quarter.

Beauty distribution, including GSSBB, reported sales of Rs 168 crore, up 59 per cent year-on-year and its highest quarterly sales, according to the company.

Customer engagement remained strong, with more than 200,000 makeovers and over 500 masterclasses conducted during the quarter.

The retailer's premium portfolio accounted for 73 per cent of sales, an increase of 390 basis points year-on-year, with sales from the portfolio growing 10 per cent. The performance underscores the company's focus on higher-value products and premium customer segments.

Department Stores And Loyalty Programme

The department store business recorded sales of Rs 1,302 crore, up 4 per cent year-on-year. Festive-adjusted like-for-like sales growth stood at 7 per cent, indicating underlying demand momentum despite the shift in festive purchases.

Shoppers Stop's First Citizen loyalty programme expanded its membership base to 14 million. Enrolments in the premium Black Card category reached a record 40,000 during the quarter, up 24 per cent year-on-year, with a renewal rate of 66 per cent. The Black Card segment contributed 22 per cent of total sales, while the programme overall accounted for 84 per cent of sales.

The retailer also continued expanding its store network. It opened seven stores during Q2, comprising four department stores, two beauty boutiques and one MAC shop-in-shop, with capital expenditure of Rs 39 crore. During the first half of FY27, it opened 15 stores with capital investment of Rs 83 crore.

INTUNE Expansion And Debt Reduction

INTUNE, the company's value-fashion format, recorded festive-adjusted like-for-like sales growth of 6 per cent year-on-year. The company reported improving productivity and fresher inventory, alongside margin expansion and lower losses in its new ventures.

The company said losses in its new ventures declined by Rs 8 crore, supported by improved INTUNE productivity and the integration of SSBeauty.in with SS.com. It expects further improvement in profitability.

Inventory discipline remained another priority. Shoppers Stop reduced outright inventory by Rs 78 crore year-on-year, while INTUNE's inventory declined by Rs 33 crore.

Net debt fell by Rs 82 crore during the quarter. The company reiterated its target of becoming debt-free by the end of Q3 FY27.

First-Half Performance

For the first half of FY27, consolidated non-GAAP revenue rose 8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 3,154 crore, while Ebitda increased 48 per cent to Rs 86 crore. PAT stood at Rs 11 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 11 crore in H1 FY26.

On a consolidated GAAP basis, revenue increased 10 per cent to Rs 2,658 crore. Ebitda rose 14 per cent to Rs 412 crore, while the net loss narrowed to Rs 11 crore from Rs 36 crore a year earlier.

The company also continued to strengthen its private-brand portfolio, expanding the availability of its premium FRATINI Girl apparel line to 95 stores and its Bandeya range to 60 stores.

data.title: L&T Finance Q2 Profit Rises 33% To Record Rs 975 Cr
data.description:
L&T Finance reported its highest-ever consolidated profit after tax of Rs 975 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 33 per cent year-on-year, supported by growth in its retail portfolio, improving asset quality and lower credit costs.

The non-banking financial company’s consolidated loan book reached a record Rs 1,36,635 crore in Q2FY27, registering 28 per cent growth from a year earlier. Its retail book expanded 29 per cent to Rs 1,34,600 crore from Rs 1,04,607 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Retail disbursements rose 27 per cent year-on-year to Rs 24,027 crore from Rs 18,883 crore. Growth was spread across rural and urban markets, with the lender continuing to expand its higher-yielding loan segments.

Personal Loans, Gold Finance Drive Growth

Personal loans recorded one of the strongest increases, with the book expanding 72 per cent year-on-year to Rs 18,664 crore from Rs 10,878 crore. Two-wheeler finance grew 24 per cent to Rs 16,158 crore, while quarterly disbursements in the segment increased 26 per cent to Rs 3,170 crore.

Gold finance recorded the sharpest expansion, with its loan book surging 242 per cent to Rs 5,043 crore from Rs 1,475 crore a year earlier. Gold loan disbursements jumped 229 per cent to Rs 3,237 crore from Rs 983 crore.

Housing loans and loans against property grew 20 per cent to Rs 32,846 crore, with quarterly disbursements rising 8 per cent to Rs 2,926 crore. The SME finance book increased 27 per cent to Rs 9,495 crore.

Rural business finance expanded 22 per cent year-on-year to Rs 33,465 crore. Farmer finance grew at a slower pace, with the book increasing 9 per cent to Rs 17,397 crore, while quarterly disbursements declined 1 per cent to Rs 1,643 crore.

L&T Finance is also increasing its focus on technology under its Lakshya 2031 strategy. Its PLANET app has crossed 2.7 crore downloads and now handles 94 per cent of customer service requests. The platform facilitated collections of Rs 2,168 crore and generated business worth Rs 5,934 crore during the quarter.

The company has introduced a dedicated rural interface for the app with multilingual capabilities, including Hindi, and has partnered with Pine Labs to introduce agentic commerce and payments on the PLANET platform.

L&T Finance said it continues to invest in artificial intelligence-led credit administration and portfolio management while expanding its distribution network across gold finance, micro loan against property, personal loans and two-wheeler finance.

data.title: Bajaj Consumer Care Appoints Jitendra Mahajan As Independent Director
data.description:
The FMCG veteran brings over three decades of experience across business transformation, supply chains, digital innovation and ESG

Bajaj Consumer Care Limited has appointed Jitendra Mahajan to its board as an Independent Director, bringing more than 30 years of experience in the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sector.

Mahajan has previously worked with Marico, Britannia and Diageo India, building experience across business leadership and transformation. His professional background includes leading businesses with revenues exceeding USD 1 billion.

His appointment adds experience in business transformation, supply chain management, digital innovation and environmental, social and governance (ESG) initiatives to the company’s board.

Experience Across FMCG

Mahajan’s career spans more than three decades in the FMCG industry, with experience across companies operating in consumer products and beverages. His previous associations with Marico, Britannia and Diageo India have given him exposure to business operations and leadership in the sector.

His experience in managing large businesses and driving transformation is relevant to areas such as operational efficiency, supply chain strategy and the adoption of digital capabilities. His background in ESG also brings experience in an area increasingly relevant to corporate governance and long-term business planning.

Board Appointment

As an Independent Director, Mahajan joins the board of Bajaj Consumer Care Limited, which operates in the consumer care segment. His appointment brings senior industry experience to the company’s board-level leadership.

Further details about his tenure, committee assignments and previous designations at Marico, Britannia and Diageo India were not included in the announcement.

data.title: Starlink Says India Infrastructure Ready, Reliance Stresses Regulatory Compliance
data.description:
Elon Musk-led Starlink says it has established dedicated infrastructure and secured requisite government approvals, as the satellite internet market awaits spectrum assignment and other operational clearances

Starlink on Friday said it was ready to provide high-speed internet services in India, claiming it had established dedicated infrastructure and secured the requisite government approvals. The statement came in response to Reliance Industries’ position that all satellite communications operators, including Starlink, must comply with Indian laws and policies.

The Elon Musk-led company made the statement on X while responding to a post by Reliance, which had said on Thursday that it welcomed competition in satellite communications but expected every operator to follow the country’s regulatory framework.

“We have worked closely with regulators, industry and operators in India for 5+ years, and built a network of dedicated systems, gateways, and other infrastructure all in-country to exclusively serve Indian traffic safely and securely — and all with the requisite government approvals. Starlink is ready to connect India with high-speed internet,” the company said.

The exchange follows a public dispute over competition and regulatory approvals in India’s satellite communications market. Musk had criticised the competitive environment, while Reliance maintained that domestic and foreign companies must operate under the same legal framework.

Reliance’s Position

In its Thursday statement, Reliance said it had never feared competition and viewed it as a test of which company served customers best. It cited the growth of its telecommunications business, Jio, since entering India’s mobile services market in 2016.

“At Reliance, we have never feared competition. We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best,” the company said.

Reliance said Jio had built a customer base of more than 530 million over the past decade, offering affordable data services and digital infrastructure.

“We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land,” it said.

The company also said India’s openness to investment and innovation depended on adherence to the rule of law. It noted that Jio’s own satellite services were awaiting clearances.

The statement followed Musk’s criticism of India’s satellite communications market. In posts on X, he accused powerful business interests of seeking to preserve a “monopolistic chokehold” on Indian consumers and sarcastically referred to Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani as “Prime Minister Ambani”, questioning his influence over government decisions.

The Ministry of Communications rejected allegations that India’s regulatory framework was unfair or discriminatory, describing such suggestions as “baseless and misconceived”. Government sources have said companies must comply with Indian laws to operate in the country.

Licences And Approvals

Starlink, Reliance’s Jio Satcom and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb are pursuing opportunities in India’s satellite communications market. Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia has said the three ventures have secured satellite communications licences, while Amazon’s Project Kuiper has also expressed interest in the market.

However, a licence alone does not permit commercial operations. Satellite operators must meet security requirements and obtain spectrum assignment under the applicable regulatory framework.

Scindia has said spectrum will be assigned after the government finalises a revenue-based charging framework and individual operators fulfil the required security conditions. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India and the Department of Telecommunications have been working towards a decision on satellite spectrum pricing.

The distinction between licensing and operational approval remains central to the dispute, with operators awaiting the clearances needed to launch commercial services.

OneWeb Awaits Clearance

The debate has also involved Bharti Airtel Chairman Sunil Mittal, whose satellite communications venture, Eutelsat OneWeb, is awaiting permission to begin commercial operations in India.

Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026, Mittal said OneWeb was ahead of Starlink in the queue for launching services in the country.

“I think I am significantly ahead in the queue from him. I applied five years back,” Mittal said. “We don’t have the permission, so we’ll be very happy to get it at least a few days before him.”

Mittal said OneWeb’s ground network had been ready for three years and its satellites had been hovering over India for five years, but the company was still awaiting permission to begin commercial operations.

Jio’s Satellite Plans

Reliance is also pursuing its satellite communications plans, including a proposed constellation of about 1,600 low-Earth-orbit satellites intended to extend internet connectivity to 600,000 villages.

The initiative could bring Jio into more direct competition with Starlink in remote areas and locations with limited terrestrial broadband coverage.

The two companies signed an agreement last year to explore ways of bringing Starlink services to Indian customers through Jio’s retail network. The arrangement adds another dimension to their evolving relationship as both companies pursue opportunities in India’s satellite internet market.

The timing of commercial launches will depend on the applicable spectrum framework, security requirements and other regulatory conditions.
